newsitem.title: UK: UK's Bradford & Bingley mum on mortgage buy.
newsitem.headline: UK's Bradford & Bingley mum on mortgage buy.

text.p: Britain's Bradford & Bingley Building Society would not be drawn on Thursday on a report it was poised to buy a mortgage business from high street heavyweight bank Lloyds TSB.
Christopher Rodrigues, the chief executive of the mutually-owned building society, declined to comment when asked if Bradford & Bingley was about to buy Mortgage Express.

The building society was named in a Financial Times report which suggested Lloyds TSB would sell the Mortgage Express business, which has assets of 1.6 billion pounds ($2.6 billion). The business is separate to Cheltenham & Gloucester, which is also owned by Lloyds TSB.

Some delegates at the annual meeting of the Building Societies Association (BSA) said they expected an announcement to be made on Friday. If Bradford & Bingley does buy Mortgage Express it could pay around 60 million pounds, they added.

Mortgage Express is a centralised mortgage lender which sold through intermediaries but stopped taking on new business at the height of the housing recession in 1991 when it was losing money at the rate of a million pounds a week.
If Bradford & Bingley did buy it, building society sources said it would have to pay around four percent of total assets.
Lloyds came to own the business through its acquisition of TSB in December 1995. A spokeswoman for the bank told Reuters she could not comment on the report, which was "market speculation".
At the end of 1996 Bradford & Bingley had total assets of around 17.0 billion pounds.
Delegates at the BSA conference pointed out that building societies were looking for ways to increase their mortgage books and acquisition was an obvious way of doing this.
But some raised questions over the quality of the Mortgage Express mortgage book, suggesting it could dilute Bradford & Bingley's own business. ($ = 0.607 British Pounds)
